Clothing & appearance 1

Shop for clothes in Thai. This first part of Clothing & appearance covers the basics — เสื้อยืด (t-shirts), กางเกงยีนส์ (jeans), a กระโปรง (skirt), รองเท้า (shoes), a หมวก (hat) — and the fitting-room ritual: asking to ลอง (try on), finding the ห้องลอง (fitting room), when something's คับ (tight) or พอดี (just right), asking for another ไซส์ (size), plus แว่นกันแดด (sunglasses), ถุงเท้า (socks) and ชุดชั้นใน (underwear). All 26 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations and word-by-word notes, so the shopping vocabulary sticks by ear.

Thai often uses kinship terms by relative age as polite address — พี่ ('older sibling') here just means someone a little older, not an actual sibling; ลุง/ป้า (uncle/auntie) and น้อง (younger) work the same way.

ใน=inห้องแอร์=air-con roomเย็น=coldจัง=soก็เลย=so thenหยิบ=grabแจ็กเก็ต=jacketมา=(to)ใส่=put on
Indoor air-conditioning in Thailand is often set very cold, so people moving from the outdoor heat into a mall, office or bus often carry a light jacket — the opposite problem to the weather outside.
